questions.question: Define the term 'multinational corporation' (MNC) and explain two benefits it might bring to a developing host country. (4 marks)

GlobalTextiles is a European clothing retailer sourcing 80% of its products from factories in Bangladesh and Cambodia. An investigation revealed some supplier factories pay below the living wage and require 60+ hour weeks. Analyse the ethical concerns associated with these supply chain practices. (6 marks)

A major technology MNC generates significant revenue from sales in several African countries but reports most of its profits in a low-tax European jurisdiction using transfer pricing between subsidiaries. Assess the impact of transfer pricing on host countries. (10 marks)
Evaluate whether the growth of multinational corporations has been a positive or negative development for the global economy. (20 marks)
Outline two reasons why a multinational corporation might locate manufacturing operations in a developing country. (4 marks)

Source A. Korvane is a sportswear MNC with its head office in Europe. It spent $120m building a shoe factory in Kestria, a lower-income country, where it employs 4,000 workers at $300 a month; local factories pay an average of $240. The factory buys $18m a year of materials and services from local firms, and two local shoemakers say they have lost skilled staff to it. Each year it exports $200m of shoes, imports $80m of components and sends $30m of profit to its head office. Kestria taxes company profits at 25%. The factory makes a pair for $20 and sells it for $22 to Korvane Trading, a subsidiary in Vessia, where profits are taxed at 5%; unrelated firms trade similar pairs at $30. It sells 5,000,000 pairs a year. Residents complain of dye in the river and smoke from the boilers; cleaner equipment would cost $6m. Korvane also buys clothing from 40 supplier factories in Kestria, and an inspection found children working at 3 of them, although its supplier code bans child labour. A video from one of them was shared widely on social media. Its "eco" range contains 10% recycled material. Korvane now plans a second factory costing $80m and employing 2,500 people, and is choosing between Kestria and a neighbouring country; Kestria's government is considering a 5-year tax holiday to win it. Explain one way Korvane's factory could affect local businesses in Kestria. (4 marks)
